gate: Control is the felt drive at the core of this code. Not domination, not the urge to crush anyone underfoot, but the practical pull to take a situation in hand and manage what is actually there. Resources, money, the small calendar of who does what on Thursday, the matter of how the household or the project actually keeps itself alive. A person carrying this gate feels uneasy in rooms where no one is steering. The hand reaches for the wheel almost before thought. Most readings of this drive go wrong at exactly this point, mistaking the reach for ego or for a need to be the boss. The reach is older than that. It is the body answering a real lack in the field, a missing hand on the rudder. The misread comes when the hand starts grabbing for the wheel even when the wheel is already held.
centre_field: The will centre is the body's small red triangle, the seat of capacity and value, the engine that backs a promise with the energy to keep it. Only about a third of people carry this centre defined, which is why the world quietly idealises something most bodies are not built for. Placement is the teaching. Control is wired here, into the motor of doing, not into the head where it could stay theoretical. The drive to manage resources runs on real fuel, which is why it can actually be enacted and which is why it burns out when it is asked to run without rest. The centre is built to work in pulses, not in a flat line. Value is its other half. The hand that reaches for the wheel is the same hand that knows the cost of what is being steered.
channel: Standing alone, this code has a problem. The drive to manage is real, but management without a tribe to manage is only restlessness with no object. The reach is toward the gate of the gatherer, the one that pulls people into a circle and holds them there as a community. The two together form the channel of money, the tribal current that takes the will to lead and the gathered group and makes them one piece of machinery. Without the other half, the controlling drive has no field to operate in, no resources actually pooled, no one looking up to be steered. It becomes a hand on an empty wheel. The gathering is what gives the steering somewhere to go. The code is built to need a tribe before its leadership becomes anything more than the private pressure of a body that wants to take charge.
